cl_can_cbd_with_thc.q: Does CBD taken with THC change THC's effects?
cl_can_cbd_with_thc.short: Studies disagree on CBD and THC; no reliable pattern has been shown across different conditions.
cl_can_cbd_with_thc.but: The studies used different amounts and timings. Most were small, and earlier trials were read through a review.
how: A review gathered 16 lab studies of healthy volunteers, from 1974 to 2019. In most, adding CBD made no clear difference to feeling high, heart rate or THC in the blood.
A few small studies, where THC was swallowed or injected, found less anxiety or fewer paranoid feelings with CBD. The review found no pattern by amount or way of taking it.
In a later trial, 18 adults ate brownies with THC alone or the same THC plus a large amount of CBD. With CBD, blood THC was higher and they felt sicker and more impaired.
Other test medicines, including a sedative, were given in that trial. They may have added to the effects.

cl_caf_panic.q: Can caffeine bring on panic attacks in people with panic disorder?
cl_caf_panic.short: About half had a panic attack after one big dose; none after a dummy.
cl_caf_panic.but: Most studies used one large amount. The review cannot show what ordinary smaller servings do.
how: A 2022 review included 10 small lab studies of adults with panic disorder during a break from psychiatric medicines.
After caffeine, 121 of 237 had a panic attack. None was reported after a dummy drink or capsule, though not everyone completed both conditions.
In studies with both groups, about 54 in 100 people with panic disorder had an attack after caffeine, against 2 in 100 without it.
Anxiety also rose more after caffeine than a dummy in all five studies that tested that comparison. The pooled anxiety result was a different comparison: change after caffeine in the two groups.

freq.title: Out of every 100 people given one large dose of caffeine in a lab, how many had a panic attack?
freq.note: Six studies with both groups: 69 of 128 people with panic disorder against 2 of 115 without it. None was reported after placebo. The caffeine-equivalent amount of one citrate-labelled study is unclear.

cl_alc_meals_bac.q: Does eating before drinking change blood alcohol?
cl_alc_meals_bac.short: In 9 men, a meal just before drinking roughly halved peak blood alcohol.
cl_alc_meals_bac.but: One small lab study of young men. It measured blood alcohol, without testing impairment.
how: Nine healthy young men were given the same small amount of alcohol on five days: after three kinds of breakfast, after a night without food, or through a drip.
After a breakfast, the highest blood alcohol was about half the level after no food: 13 to 18 against 31 mg per 100 ml.
The kind of breakfast made no clear difference, but the study was too small to tell.
After food, blood alcohol varied more from person to person. Larger amounts, women and other meals were not studied.

cl_alc_protective_strategies.q: Do habits meant to make drinking less harmful help?
cl_alc_protective_strategies.short: Teaching students bundles of these habits changed drinking very little; individual habits were not tested.
cl_alc_protective_strategies.but: No trial tested one habit on its own, and most were US students.
how: A 2026 review included 15 trials, mostly of US college students; 11 contributed to its main pooled results.
Students who were taught them drank very slightly less often. How much they drank did not clearly change.
In surveys, students who said they used more habits also said they drank less. But they were asked about both at the same time.
Day by day, students drank more on days they had a sober driver or went home with a friend. The author thinks they planned these for heavy nights.
